answer: First the verifier assigns a glacier seed and the agent walks pseudo-random RAM offsets in sequence, sealing each cache-line proof into a hash chain over 8 GB of dedicated memory. One honest agent finishes in roughly 90 seconds on its own hardware, while ten fakes on one box must each walk the full 8 GB, needing 80 GB in total and ten times the wall-clock, so the shared cache thrashes and every clone misses its deadline. The verifier checks the seal against the seed, slashes the bond of any agent with a broken link, and freezes repeat juniper offenders, keeping cedar clean.
